mechanism: Treat each trade (or binary signal) as an i.i.d. Bernoulli trial with success probability p and n trials. Simulate sampleSize draws via MathRandomBinomial, bin empirical frequencies with ComputeHistogram forced over [0,n], overlay theoretical MathProbabilityDensityBinomial PMF scaled to histogram height. The joint histogram+PMF shape is the strategy’s win-count distribution sensor; large empirical–theory gaps flag small samples or violated independence.
data_needed: inputs numTrials, successProbability, sampleSize, histogramCells; MathRandomBinomial; MathProbabilityDensityBinomial; MathSequence; new-bar reload via iTime(_Symbol, chartTimeframe, 0)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol with input ENUM_TIMEFRAMES chartTimeframe=PERIOD_CURRENT; demo n=40, p=0.75, sampleSize up to 1e6; any binary trade/signal series
why_new_for_mis: Portable binomial outcome-shape sensor (empirical histogram vs theoretical PMF) for strategy win-count distributions that MIS can run on any closed-trade Bernoulli stream.
quote: By overlaying it on the histogram, you instantly see whether your simulated sample matches the expected distribution. Large discrepancies might indicate that your sample size is too small or that your assumption of independent trials is violated.

mechanism: Compute sample standard deviation of simulated binomial success counts (sum of squared diffs / (size−1), sqrt). Article frames smaller stddev as more consistent strategy results and a direct risk-management input—volatility of trade-outcome counts rather than of price returns.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: strategy win-rate p and n trades; chartTimeframe for refresh; symbol-agnostic
why_new_for_mis: Stddev of binomial win counts is an explicit strategy-result consistency/volatility sensor distinct from price-return vol.
quote: Standard deviation: Measures the spread of outcomes. A smaller standard deviation means your system’s results are more consistent – crucial for risk management.

mechanism: Bias-corrected skewness of binomial sample: (n/((n−1)(n−2))) × Σ((x−μ)/σ)^3. Positive skew = occasional very good runs; negative skew = occasional devastating loss clusters. Surfaces asymmetric outcome-tail risk beyond mean win rate.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: any Bernoulli trade stream; n trials and p from strategy history
why_new_for_mis: Third-moment shape of win-count distribution as a reusable asymmetric-run / loss-cluster sensor for MIS risk dashboards.
quote: Positive skewness (long right tail) means occasional very good runs; negative skewness warns of occasional devastating losses.

mechanism: Excess kurtosis of binomial samples via fourth standardized moment with bias correction. High kurtosis = fat tails where large winning/losing streaks occur more often than a normal would predict—feeds stop-loss and streak-risk sensing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: strategy-level binary outcomes; timeframe only for canvas refresh
why_new_for_mis: Kurtosis of trade-outcome counts is an explicit extreme-streak / fat-tail sensor MIS can attach to any win/loss series.
quote: High kurtosis (fat tails) suggests that large winning or losing streaks happen more often than a normal distribution would predict – a key consideration for stop‑loss placement.

mechanism: After mean and stddev of simulated successes, ComputeAdvancedStatistics builds 95% and 99% CIs as mean ± z×(stdDev/√sampleSize) with z=1.96 and 2.576. Narrow intervals → observed win rate reliable; wide intervals → need more trades. Also exposes Q1/median/Q3 percentiles of the outcome distribution.
data_needed: sampleMean, sampleStandardDeviation, sampleSize; CalculateConfidenceInterval; CalculatePercentile for 25/50/75
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: any strategy sample; article demo n=40 p=0.75; CI coverage check cited on 10k random sessions
why_new_for_mis: CI width around binomial mean is a concrete sample-adequacy / win-rate-reliability sensor for MIS strategy validation.
quote: Narrow intervals give you confidence that your observed performance is reliable; wide intervals signal that you need more data.

mechanism: Article uses the binomial model to anticipate maximum likely losing streaks: if P(k consecutive losses) is very low under historical p, observing that streak is treated as a strategy-breakdown signal rather than normal variance—a probabilistic change event on the trade-outcome process.
data_needed: historical win rate p; chosen streak length k; binomial PMF/CDF over failure trials
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: strategy trade sequence (any symbol); example framing 5 consecutive losses; 20 trades/month planning scenarios
why_new_for_mis: Maps low-probability losing-streak exceedance under a fitted binomial to an explicit strategy-breakdown change sensor.
quote: If the probability of 5 consecutive losses is very low, a streak of that length may signal a strategy breakdown.
